what_actually_failed.runs: run 36296142410 attempt 1 and attempt 2 (a re-run of the same gate, not a bypass), both failure, both at Makefile verify-gpu-regressions
what_actually_failed.assertion: TestSubscribeWithContextDone at client_test.go:424, require.Eventually over a process-wide goroutine count, 21.00s in attempt 2 (the full 20s window)
what_actually_failed.observed_values: the failure messages read 15 with baseline 16, and 21 with baseline 16. Both numbers come from the argument evaluated when Eventually is called, not at the deadline, so they say the count differed from the baseline at the start of the window; the old logs contain no stack byte counts and no dump

proven: the same assertion failed twice on the runner; that is a repeat failure of one assertion, not a proof of determinism, and not a proof that a resource actually leaked

the baseline was polluted by construction: clientSubscriptionGoroutines() counted every goroutine in the process whose stack mentions sse.(*Client)., and the package's earlier cases leave such goroutines behind, so the sampled baseline was 16 while this case had contributed 20 more (10 subscriptions plus their 10 readLoop goroutines, as the rewritten logs measure); a baseline that moves during the window cannot be satisfied by any equality

the earlier 'ok ... (cached)' line in the push run meant that package never executed in that job, so 'the same tree passed on push' was not evidence of anything; that is why the gate line now carries -count=1

a truncated stack dump is a real hazard, just not this one's proven cause: the new collector measured 65750 bytes of stacks in this process, so a 64KiB buffer truncates and had to grow to 128KiB, while the old fixed 1MiB buffer was not truncated locally
not_proven: truncation is not established as the root cause of the runner failure, because the old buffer was 1MiB and the measured dump is ~65KiB

no claim is made that production leaks: after the repair, ten subscriptions on a live stream that were each proven to be receiving exited 90-175 microseconds after the cancellation with err=nil, requests seen 10, server-side streams still open 0, and no sse.(*Client). goroutine left in the isolated child
attribution.production_path_examined_without_changin: SubscribeWithContext wraps its operation in backoff.RetryNotify with a nil ReconnectStrategy, i.e. a fresh ExponentialBackOff whose MaxElapsedTime is about 15 minutes. readLoop turns io.EOF into a nil error, which ends the retry and returns; any other read or request error re-enters the retry loop instead of stopping. Cancelling before the request is established, or a transport that reports context cancellation rather than EOF on the body, therefore parks the subscription in reconnection backoff rather than returning it. Nothing was changed here: no forced StopBackOff, no reconnect strategy edit, no protocol, auth or buffering parameter touched. If a run ever shows a subscription that was ready with a normal handler still failing to return, that is a production finding to be filed with its stacks, not something this test may hide

repair.production_files_diff: empty, verified by git diff --name-only filtered to everything except those two paths
kept_from_the_original_case: the real Client over a real HTTP event stream
the same context cancellation as the trigger
what_it_measures_now: readiness: every one of the ten reports from inside its own handler after it has actually received an event, before the cancellation is issued; a sleep is no longer the gate
completion: ten distinct numbered returns inside the window; a duplicate, an out-of-range or a missing return fails, so fewer exits elsewhere cannot cancel out a leak

its own server-side resources: the fixture counts requests and streams still open at the deadline, which is how a readLoop that never noticed the cancellation shows up without borrowing another case's goroutines

residue only where ownership is unambiguous: the same scenario re-executes as a child process of this very test binary running nothing else, where any remaining sse.(*Client). stack must belong to it; -race is inherited because it is the same binary

the forced shutdown order is last: the verdict is taken before the publisher stops and before the httptest server closes its connections, so closing the server cannot make a non-exiting implementation look correct
repair.stack_collector: starts at a requested size and doubles until the dump covers runtime.NumGoroutine() goroutines and has room left; an incomplete dump is reported as incomplete and is never parsed, and reaching the 16MiB ceiling fails rather than returning a comfortable empty set
controls_added: withholding one completion fails the ten-of-ten wait, and the wait returns at its deadline instead of running on
one subscription reporting twice fails: ten distinct exits are required
a raw 64 byte snapshot is refused as incomplete while the growing collector reaches a complete dump with a larger buffer

the leak probe: an eleventh subscription on a context that is never cancelled makes the isolated child fail, and the failure names what outlived the cancellation; the probe is released only after the verdict

early_return_rejection.defect_in_the_previous_patch: watchReady counted readiness only, collectCompletions counted distinct indexes, and the judgement looked at ready count plus waitErr; subOutcome carried a timestamp that was never compared with the cancellation moment, so ten subscriptions that all returned before cancel() - and were then collected as ten distinct "completions" with zero residue - would have passed
early_return_rejection.mechanism: watchReady selects on readiness and completions together and returns errEarlyReturn as soon as an owned index reports before the cancellation; report.cancelledAt is recorded exactly once, immediately before cancel(), and collectCompletions stamps each return with afterCancel = at.After(cancelledAt); acceptanceOwnSignals fails on any early set, on fewer than ten distinct owned indexes, and on any completion recorded without the cancellation having been issued
early_return_rejection.index_discipline: readiness and completion both accept only the ten unique indexes 0..9 owned by the scenario; a duplicate adds nothing and an outside index - the leak probe is number 10 - cannot stand in for a missing one, so nine owned plus the probe plus a repeat is reported as nine and fails
early_return_rejection.error_contract: no assertion is made about the returned error being nil or matching any text: what is verified is actual readiness, exit after the cancellation, and resource closure, so the production return contract stays untouched

shared_client.restored: NewClient is called once outside the start loop and all ten subscriptions share that instance and the same context, as the case at b3ce1df had it; the per-index once, readiness and completion signals stay
shared_client.probe_client: the deliberately-open eleventh subscription used by the negative control gets its own Client, so it can never substitute for the shared instance the ten share
shared_client.race_evidence: with the shared instance the target case passed -race -count=3 with 0 DATA RACE, so no production synchronisation or reconnect change was needed or made
shared_client.stream_argument: the original case subscribed to the stream named "test" and so does this one; the shared fixture now checks the incoming request actually carries stream=test, so the wire shape is verified rather than assumed, and the earlier version of the repair had quietly subscribed with an empty stream

controls: one subscription completing before the cancellation fails, even with a full post-cancel set and clean resources behind it
all ten completing before the cancellation fails for the same reason, and the resource and residue halves are asserted clean in that same case so the rejection can only come from the early exits
nine owned readiness signals plus the probe index plus a duplicate are counted as nine and fail
a withheld or a duplicated completion fails the collection
a raw 64 byte snapshot is refused as incomplete and the growing collector has to reach a complete dump
the leak probe child must fail naming what outlived the cancellation, and the control also asserts it did not fail for readiness or for an early return, so it cannot pass for the wrong reason
